speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation; to begin my assessment, are you currently experiencing any headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The combination of fever, altered mentation, and a history of haloperidol use in a patient with tics is highly suggestive of NMS, even in the absence of reported neck stiffness. I will proceed with a physical exam focusing on rigidity and blood pressure, and request labs for CK and electrolytes to confirm.
